title: Coddy config.yaml
description: Configuration file for the Coddy agent (default location: ~/.coddy/config.yaml). Reference: https://coddy.dev/docs/reference/config. Any string value may reference environment variables with ${VAR_NAME}. ${CODDY_HOME} is expanded by the loader; ${CWD} stays in the value and is expanded per session by whatever reads the path (skills.dirs, subagents.dirs, hooks.files, prompts.dir), except in the process-scoped sessions.dir, memory.dir and logger.file, where it means the default working directory. MCP servers are not declared here: they live in <home>/mcp.json and the project's .coddy/mcp.json, and an old mcp_servers key is moved into <home>/mcp.json on load.

providers.title: LLM providers
providers.description: API credentials and transport selection for upstream LLM vendors. When api_key is empty, the runtime reads the NAME_API_KEY environment variable (NAME is the provider name in uppercase with hyphens mapped to underscores); a row of type "codex" signs in with ChatGPT and reads no key.

name.description: Logical id used as the first segment of models[].model. ASCII letters, digits, hyphen, underscore; must start with a letter.

type.description: Wire protocol for this provider. Use "openai" for configurable OpenAI-compatible endpoints (OpenAI, DeepSeek, Groq, Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio), "anthropic" for Anthropic, "neuraldeep" for NeuralDeep's OpenAI-compatible API at one of its two official deployments (selected with api_base), "codex" for ChatGPT OAuth against the official Codex backend (Responses API), or "devin" for a Devin (Cognition) account signed in through the browser or the Devin CLI, served by the Devin API server; see https://coddy.dev/docs/features/devin, or "coddy" for a model that another Coddy shares (its models[].shared_as): api_base is the address of that remote coddy serve, or of a swarm relay mount, and every model turn is one streamed call to it.

api_base.description: Optional base URL override. For type "openai" include /v1 (e.g. http://localhost:11434/v1); for type "anthropic" an Anthropic-compatible gateway (default https://api.anthropic.com). For type "neuraldeep" it selects the deployment: https://api.neuraldeep.ru/v1 (Russia, the default) or https://api.neuraldeep.tech/v1 (the international mirror); any other value falls back to the default. Ignored for types "codex" and "devin", which always use their official endpoints. Required for type "coddy": the origin of the remote coddy serve (https://host:12345) or of a swarm relay mount (https://relay/swarm/nodes/<node>), an http or https URL; the type appends /coddy/llm/... to it. A plain http:// address whose host is not loopback sends the token and the whole conversation in clear text, and coddy -t warns about it.

api_key.description: Provider secret. A literal key, a "${ENV}" reference expanded at load time, or empty to read NAME_API_KEY at LLM call time. Resolution order: api_key -> api_key_command stdout -> NAME_API_KEY. For type "devin" it is a Devin session token and, when set, wins over the browser login and the Devin CLI login. Ignored for type "codex", which signs in with ChatGPT. For type "coddy" it is the token the remote accepts (a shared-model token is enough), or the relay's client token through a mount; leave it empty for a remote without authentication.

api_key_command.description: Optional credential-helper command. When api_key is empty it runs via the detected host shell (pwsh, powershell, or cmd on Windows; bash or sh elsewhere) and the trimmed stdout is used as the key. On failure resolution falls back to NAME_API_KEY. Never run for type "codex", which takes no key.

proxy.description: inherit (the default, the same as leaving the key out), none, or a proxy URL: http://, https://, socks5:// or socks5h://. inherit follows the proxy the environment of the Coddy process names - HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY and NO_PROXY, never for a loopback address; ALL_PROXY is not read. none connects directly and ignores those variables. A proxy URL sends every request of this row through that proxy, NO_PROXY and loopback included; with SOCKS the proxy resolves host names. The setting covers every request of the provider: its completions, its model list, its account usage and its sign-in.

timeout_ms.description: Optional bound on each LLM HTTP request to this provider, including the streamed body read. 0 (the default) sets no client timeout, so slow prompt processing on large contexts is never cut short.

busy_wait_ms.description: How long, in milliseconds, one call to a provider of type coddy waits for a free slot of the remote when the remote answers busy (it runs at most httpserver.shared_models.max_streams calls per credential at once). A value above zero wins; 0 or absent falls back to agent.shared_busy_wait_ms, which is 30000 unless set. Other provider types ignore it.

ca_file.description: Provider of type coddy only: PEM bundle of the certificate authority that signed the remote's (or the relay's) certificate, besides the system roots. Another provider type refuses the key.

client_cert_file.description: Provider of type coddy only: PEM client certificate presented to the remote or the relay when it asks for one (mutual TLS). Set together with client_key_file. Read at each handshake, so a rotated certificate is used by the next connection. Another provider type refuses the key.

client_key_file.description: Provider of type coddy only: PEM private key of client_cert_file. A path: the key itself never goes in the configuration. Another provider type refuses the key.

usage_limits_panel.description: Show this provider's account usage panel (the console footer line and /usage, the usage section and banner in the web UI) and read the provider's usage endpoint for it (GET /v1/limits for type neuraldeep, the Codex backend's usage endpoint for type codex, the seat-management status RPC for type devin, and for type coddy the account of the remote Coddy behind each model, read through that remote). Omit or true keeps the panel on; false hides it and stops those reads for this row. Only providers whose type has a usage source are affected.

models.title: Logical models
models.description: Named model entries the agent and UI can select.

model.description: "provider_name/api_model_id": the first path segment must match a providers[].name; the remainder is sent to the LLM API (may itself contain slashes).

max_tokens.description: Upper bound on completion tokens per assistant message. A codex model never sends it (the Codex backend rejects max_output_tokens), so there it bounds nothing, and coddy -t and --dry-run warn about such a value.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature (0 = deterministic; higher = more random).

max_context_tokens.description: Context window of the model in tokens: what the web UI context ring, the console context percentage and the automatic compaction trigger measure against. 0 reads it from the provider's model listing when the provider reports one (the NeuralDeep hub, vLLM, OpenRouter, LM Studio), else 128000.

multimodal.description: Model accepts image/file inputs in addition to text; the UI shows a file attachment button for this model, and read shows it the picture in a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP file instead of refusing it as binary. Absent (or null) is false, except for a model of a provider of type coddy, where the remote's listing decides; a written value, false included, wins over the listing.

reasoning_levels.description: Override the reasoning levels offered for this model. Omit to auto-detect from the model id (gpt-5* -> minimal,low,medium,high; OpenAI o-series, gpt-oss*, qwen3*, and Claude extended-thinking models -> low,medium,high). An explicit empty list hides the selector. Settings fills this field from GET /coddy/config/reasoning-levels behind its Fetch reasoning levels button. For a model of a provider of type coddy there is no id to detect from: omitting the key means the remote's listing decides, and a written list, an empty one included, wins.

reasoning_default.description: Reasoning level pre-selected for new chats; must be one of the resolved levels, otherwise ignored. Empty on a model of a provider of type coddy follows the remote's default.

allow_reasoning_off.description: Expose Off in the reasoning selector for this model. Enable it only when this provider/model deployment honours Coddy's provider-specific request that disables reasoning; Coddy cannot verify that capability automatically. Absent (or null) is false, except for a model of a provider of type coddy, where the remote's listing decides; a written value, false included, wins over the listing.

stream.description: Transport used to talk to this model. Omit (or true) to stream over SSE. false issues one blocking completion request and delivers the whole answer at once, for servers or proxies that handle event streams badly. Rejected for providers of type codex, whose backend is streaming-only.

shared_as.description: Offers this model to other Coddys that reach this server, under this alias: the only name that leaves the host, in the listing, in requests and in errors, never the provider/model selector. Empty or absent keeps the model private. 1 to 64 letters, digits, dots, underscores or hyphens, starting with a letter or a digit; unique across models; not allowed on a model of a provider of type coddy. The shared routes need a credential: httpserver.shared_models.tokens (opens only the LLM routes) or httpserver.auth_token; coddy -t reports shared_as without one as an error. The alias is a name, not an access boundary: the main token still reaches every model by its selector on the rest of the API.

shared_subscription_ack.description: Required next to shared_as on a model whose credential is a subscription login: providers of type codex and devin, and a neuraldeep provider with no api_key, api_key_command or NAME_API_KEY (the stored hub login fills in). Sharing a login hands its quota to every holder of a shared-model token and may breach the vendor's terms; without this key the configuration is refused at load. It has no effect without shared_as.

agent.title: ReAct agent loop
agent.description: Defaults for the main agent loop (model id and safety caps).

queue_mode.description: Preferred queue mode for Enter during a running turn: steer joins the next ReAct step, after_turn starts a new turn after the current answer. When absent, interactive surfaces ask on first use.

model.description: Optional default models[].model id. Interactive surfaces (web UI, console) pick a model per session; unattended calls that name no model (coddy -p, coddy acp, API requests without a model selector) need it set - they report 'no model configured' when it is empty.

max_turns.description: Cap on the ReAct steps (LLM calls) of one prompt turn. Defaults to 165; set 0 to disable the cap. A turn that reaches the cap ends with a notice that names it.

llm_retry_max.description: Extra attempts shared by transport retries, empty-answer recovery and first-token re-issues until tool progress or a new follow-up. 0 disables these retries. Loop guards, Stop hooks, fallback models and quota-reset waits have separate limits.

llm_retry_base_ms.description: Initial backoff between LLM retries, in milliseconds. A server-provided pause (Retry-After-Ms / Retry-After headers, "Limit resets at" / "retry in Ns" body phrases) overrides the exponential backoff, capped at 60s.

llm_min_interval_ms.description: Minimum gap between consecutive LLM calls in milliseconds, retry attempts included (0 disables pacing; e.g. 12000 on strict free tiers).

llm_first_token_timeout_ms.description: How long a streamed LLM call may stay silent before the turn cancels it (the API hang guard). An explicit 0 disables the guard; blocking (stream: false) transports are never guarded.

llm_stream_idle_timeout_ms.description: How long a streamed LLM response may send nothing after its first bytes before the stream is cut as stalled (the mid-answer hang guard): the text already delivered is kept and the turn ends with the stall named. An explicit 0 disables the guard; the wait for the first byte belongs to llm_first_token_timeout_ms, and blocking (stream: false) transports are never guarded.

loop_guard.description: Runaway-loop protection: cut a streamed response that degenerates into repeating itself, and block a tool called over and over with identical arguments.

loop_tool_repeat_limit.description: Consecutive identical tool calls in successive ReAct responses (same name, same canonical arguments) before the loop guard steps in. 0 disables the tool-repeat check.

loop_stream_repeat_cycles.description: Identical back-to-back output cycles inside one streamed response before the stream is cut. 0 disables the stream check.

loop_nudge_max.description: How many times one turn may be nudged back on track before the loop guard stops it with a notice.

wait_for_limit_reset.description: Wait for a hit usage limit to lift and re-issue the call, instead of ending the turn with the provider's error. Applies to a top-level turn whose provider names a pause beyond the retry budget (a 429 with Retry-After or "Limit resets at"); the turn lock and the client stream stay open while it waits, so it is off by default.

wait_for_limit_reset_max_ms.description: Longest time one turn spends waiting for limits in total, in milliseconds, the retry wrapper's own sleeps on a limit included; a pause that would exceed it ends the turn at once with the error. An explicit 0 never waits.

shared_busy_wait_ms.description: How long, in milliseconds, a call to a provider of type coddy waits for a free slot of the remote when it answers busy, unless the provider's own busy_wait_ms (above zero) says otherwise. Omit for 30000; an explicit 0 means no waiting: the call fails at the first busy answer. The wait is bounded, shown while it lasts and cut by Stop.

prompts.title: System prompt templates
prompts.description: Override the built-in system prompt templates (Go text/template).

dir.description: Directory containing prompt template files. Empty uses embedded defaults. Supports ~ and ${CWD} (session cwd at render time).

agent_prompt.description: File name inside prompts.dir for agent mode.

plan_prompt.description: File name inside prompts.dir for plan mode.

ask_prompt.description: File name inside prompts.dir for ask mode.

instructions.title: Project instructions
instructions.description: Files the operator adds to the system prompt (AGENTS.md convention), after the documents every session reads anyway: the AGENTS.md and DESIGN.md of the agent home, then those of the session folder, and the nested ones of a folder a tool enters, none of which is named here or can be turned off. A file already in the prompt is not read twice. See https://coddy.dev/docs/features/rules.

files.description: Extra instruction files, appended after the AGENTS.md and DESIGN.md documents in the order listed; empty by default. ${CODDY_HOME}, ${CWD} and a leading ~ expand; an absolute entry is read as it stands, a relative one resolves against the session CWD. An entry naming a document the prompt already carries is skipped.

skills.title: Skills
skills.description: Directories scanned for skills (SKILL.md and root .md/.mdc files).

dirs.description: Extra skill directories, read after the four default folders and stronger than them. The defaults are always read, lowest priority first: ${HOME}/.agents/skills (shared with every agent, npx skills and npx skillsbd install there), the project's .agents/skills, ${CODDY_HOME}/skills (Coddy's own and installed skills), the project's .coddy/skills; then these entries in their order. A skill found in several directories is taken from the last one in this order, and a directory named twice is read at its last place. ${CODDY_HOME} expands when the file is loaded, ${HOME} and ~ to your home folder, ${CWD} and a relative path against the session's workspace (the folder a new chat picked included).

project_trust.title: Project marketplaces
project_trust.description: Trust policy for the project's .coddy/marketplaces.json, which travels with the checkout: "ask" (default) leaves its sources and marketplaces out of every sync until the operator approves that exact entry for that workspace; "allow" treats them like the operator's own ${CODDY_HOME}/marketplaces.json; "deny" never uses them (they are listed as switched off). What they install goes to ${CODDY_HOME}/skills. The project's skill folders (.coddy/skills, .agents/skills) are not affected. Skill marketplaces are not declared in config.yaml: they live in ${CODDY_HOME}/marketplaces.json and the project's .coddy/marketplaces.json, and an old skills.sources list is moved into the home file on load. See https://coddy.dev/docs/features/skills#project-marketplaces-and-trust.

auto_discovery.title: Skill auto-discovery
auto_discovery.description: Offer the model-driven load_skill tool so the agent pulls a catalogued skill's full instructions into a turn on its own when the request matches, instead of requiring an explicit /name. Defaults to true.

rules.title: Project rules
rules.description: Discovery of rule files from ${CODDY_HOME}/rules (the operator's own, applied in every workspace) and from one project folder under the session CWD, the first of .coddy/rules, .agents/rules, .cursor/rules, .claude/rules, .codex/rules that holds a rule file; .mdc files are Cursor rules, .md files Claude Code rules. The AGENTS.md and DESIGN.md documents are not rules in this sense and none of these settings turns them off. See https://coddy.dev/docs/features/rules.

auto_discover.description: Scan the rule folders automatically: ${CODDY_HOME}/rules and the project folder of the session CWD. The AGENTS.md and DESIGN.md documents are read either way.

systems.description: Restrict which rule systems are loaded: user (${CODDY_HOME}/rules), coddy, agents-dir (.agents/rules), cursor, claude, codex. Empty means all. A project folder left out drops out of the chain; of the ones admitted, the first that holds a rule file is read. agents, which used to switch the nested AGENTS.md files, no longer affects them (they are always read); it is still accepted, and a list holding only agents loads no rule folder.

mcp.title: MCP discovery
mcp.description: MCP settings that are not tied to a single server entry.

project_trust.description: Trust policy for the project-local <cwd>/.coddy/mcp.json, which travels with the checkout: "ask" keeps its servers cold until the operator approves that exact declaration for that workspace; "allow" starts them automatically (trusted workspaces only); "deny" never loads them.

idle_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds an MCP server that no session holds any more keeps running before Coddy stops it: a project server once the last session of its workspace let it go, a server an ACP client sent once the last session that sent it closed. A session that takes the server in the meantime finds it running. The global servers that coddy serve, the console and coddy acp start with the process are not affected, and a server switched off, no longer approved, removed or declared differently stops at once. 0 stops a server as soon as the last session lets it go.

tools.title: Tools and permissions
tools.description: Filesystem and shell policy for built-in tools.

permission_mode.description: When the agent asks for user approval: "ask" prompts for commands and file writes; "accept_edits" auto-approves writes but prompts for commands; "bypass" never asks (trusted environments only). A session may switch its own mode until the process restarts (/permissions, the composer chip, the permission dialog); the switch is never written here.

command_allowlist.description: Commands that never require permission. Exact or prefix match (prefix + space + any args). "*" allows all commands.

ssh_connect_timeout.description: TCP dial timeout for SSH connections (ssh_run_command tool), in seconds.

output_limits.title: Tool output limits
output_limits.description: Maximum lines each tool result or error may return into the LLM context. Every enabled limit also applies a 64 KiB per-call byte safety ceiling so a huge single line cannot bypass it. 0 disables both limits for that tool. Unset fields fall back to the built-in defaults.

read.description: Max lines for a read file page or directory listing.

grep.description: Max path:line:content records returned by grep.

print_tree.description: Max lines of a directory tree.

run_command.description: Max combined stdout+stderr lines of a shell command.

ssh_run_command.description: Max combined stdout+stderr lines of a remote SSH command.

webfetch.description: Max lines of fetched page markdown.

default.description: Applies to any tool not named above, including MCP tools. 0 means unlimited.

background.title: Background tasks
background.description: Commands the agent runs detached in the session task pool instead of blocking a turn. The pool dies with the coddy process; each task's metadata and captured output stay in the session bundle, and a task interrupted by a restart is reported as orphaned.

enable.description: Offer the background option on run_command and expose the background task tools.

max_concurrent.description: How many background tasks one session may run at once. 0 uses the default.

default_timeout_seconds.description: Hard limit for a task started without an explicit timeout and without a duration estimate. 0 uses the default.

max_timeout_seconds.description: Ceiling applied to any requested or estimate-derived timeout. 0 uses the default.

output_buffer_bytes.description: How much of each task's output stays in memory for the status ticker. The full log is still written to the session bundle. 0 uses the default.

preview_server.title: Preview server
preview_server.description: The preview_server tool: a static file server the agent starts over a project directory, on a free port, so the operator can open HTML, JS and CSS work in a browser. The server is a background task of the session and runs until it is stopped, the session is deleted or coddy exits.

enable.description: Offer the preview_server tool. The server is a background task, so tools.background.enable: false turns it off as well.

host.description: Address the server binds, without a port: the port is always a free one. Anything that is not loopback exposes the served directory to whoever can reach that address.

public_host.description: Host written into the URL the agent hands out, for a coddy that runs where the operator's browser is not (a container, a remote machine). Empty uses the bind host.

websearch.title: Web search
websearch.description: Which search engines the websearch tool asks, in what order their results merge, and what it may spend asking them. Each engine reports its own outcome next to the results, so a blocked backend is named rather than counted as "the web has nothing".

engines.description: Search engines to ask, in merge order. Unset asks brave then bing. "ddg" and "google" are not asked by default: measured from a server, DuckDuckGo answers every query with an anti-bot interstitial and Google renders its results in the browser. "searxng" needs searxng_url.

engine_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds one engine may take before it is reported as unavailable. 0 uses the default.

total_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds the whole search may take, however many engines it asks. 0 uses the default.

max_concurrent_engines.description: How many engines are asked at once. 0 uses the default.

snippet_chars.description: Maximum characters of one result description. 0 uses the default.

cache_ttl_seconds.description: Seconds one engine answer is reused before the engine is asked again, so a repeated search does not repeat the request. 0 uses the default; a negative value turns caching off.

searxng_url.description: Base address of your own SearXNG instance, asked over its JSON API (enable the json format in its settings.yml). A self-hosted aggregator is the durable answer to a scraped engine being turned away; localhost and LAN addresses are allowed on purpose.

brave_api_key.description: Brave Search API subscription token. With it the brave engine uses the official JSON API instead of reading the public result page, which has no parser to break when Brave redeploys. Empty reads the BRAVE_API_KEY environment variable (also from ${CODDY_HOME}/.env), so the key need not be stored here.

http_request.title: HTTP requests
http_request.description: Policy of the http_request tool, the agent's curl: the destinations it reaches without asking and the headers every request sends. Under permission_mode ask or accept_edits a request asks the operator unless its destination is allowed here or was approved in the session; bypass never asks. See https://coddy.dev/docs/features/http-requests.

allowlist.description: Destinations a request reaches without asking: a host (api.github.com), a subdomain wildcard (*.example.com), either with an optional :port, an origin (http://localhost:8080) or an address prefix (https://api.example.com/v1/). "*" allows every destination. An entry also covers the files a request uploads and an unchecked certificate; a proxy needs an entry of its own, and a file the response is saved to follows the write policy.

default_headers.description: Headers every http_request call sends unless the call names the header itself: a browser User-Agent for a site that turns tools away, an Accept an internal service expects. They take the place of the tool's own defaults (its coddy-agent User-Agent), a call's headers take the place of them - an empty value in the call removes one - and an empty value here leaves the header out of every call that does not set it. A name is letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter. Host, Content-Type, Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding describe a single request and are refused, and so are the hop-by-hop headers (Connection, Keep-Alive, Proxy-Connection, TE, Trailer, Upgrade) and Proxy-Authorization, which an https request would carry through the proxy's tunnel to every origin. The headers go to every destination the tool reaches, so a credential here reaches all of them; the permission prompt names them and shows the value only of one that describes the client (User-Agent, Accept...), config_get keeps their values from the model, and webfetch, URL mentions and the model providers never send them. See https://coddy.dev/docs/features/http-requests#default-headers.

subagents.title: Subagents
subagents.description: User-defined child agents the model can delegate to with spawn_agent. Definitions are markdown files with YAML frontmatter; each run is a background task of the parent session with its own child session and transcript. See https://coddy.dev/docs/features/subagents.

enable.description: Register the spawn_agent tool and list the subagent catalog in the system prompt.

dirs.description: Extra definition directories, read after the four default folders and stronger than them. The defaults are always read, lowest priority first: ${HOME}/.agents/agents, the project's .agents/agents, ${CODDY_HOME}/agents, the project's .coddy/agents; then these entries in their order. A definition found in several directories is taken from the last one in this order, and a directory named twice is read at its last place. ${CODDY_HOME} expands when the file is loaded, ${HOME} and ~ to your home folder, ${CWD} and a relative path against the session's workspace. Directories inside the workspace are project scope and follow the trust policy.

project_trust.description: Trust policy for definitions found inside the workspace, which travel with the checkout: "ask" loads them but refuses to spawn one until the operator approved that exact file for that workspace (the shield in Settings -> Subagents, coddy agents trust on the machine running coddy, or POST /coddy/subagents/{name}/trust with the session workspace as cwd); "allow" treats them like the operator's own files; "deny" never reads them.

max_concurrent.description: How many subagent runs the whole process may have in flight at once, whatever session started them. Starting past the limit is refused, not queued. 0 uses the default.

max_depth.description: How deep spawning may nest: 1 lets a session spawn subagents that cannot spawn further; 0 forbids spawning everywhere. Omit for the default.

default_timeout_seconds.description: Hard limit for one run whose definition and call give no timeout. Capped by tools.background.max_timeout_seconds. 0 uses the default.

max_turns.description: ReAct rounds a child may take. 0 follows agent.max_turns.

hooks.title: Hooks
hooks.description: Operator commands run at lifecycle points of a session: before and after a tool call, when a prompt is submitted, when the agent stops, on session start and around compaction. Definitions are JSON files in the Claude Code shape (~/.coddy/hooks.json, .coddy/hooks.json, .claude/settings*.json). See https://coddy.dev/docs/features/hooks.

enable.description: Load and run hooks at all.

files.description: Definition files, lowest priority first; every matching hook runs. ${CODDY_HOME} and ${CWD} expand; a relative entry resolves against the session cwd. Files inside the workspace are project scope and follow project_trust; only the hooks key of a Claude Code settings file is read.

project_trust.description: Trust policy for hook files found inside the workspace, which travel with the checkout: "ask" lists them but runs nothing until the operator approved that exact file for that workspace on the machine running coddy (coddy hooks trust there, or POST /coddy/hooks/trust with the session workspace as cwd); "allow" treats them like the operator's own file; "deny" never reads them.

default_timeout_seconds.description: Hard limit for one hook process whose definition gives no timeout. 0 uses the default.

stop_loop_limit.description: How many times per turn a Stop hook may send the agent back to work. 0 uses the default.

max_output_chars.description: Cap on the context, messages and reasons one hook may hand to the model or the user; longer values are truncated with a marker. 0 uses the default.

logger.title: Logging
logger.description: Process log level, outputs, format, and file rotation.

level.description: Minimum severity written to the configured outputs ("warning" is accepted as an alias of "warn").

levels.description: Per-component minimum severity. A component is the dotted name a record carries in its "component" attribute (gateway, gateway.telegram, session, agent, scheduler); a parent name covers everything nested under it and the longest configured prefix wins. Records with no component follow "level".

outputs.description: Where log records go; any combination of stdout, stderr, file. Empty means stderr only.

file.description: Path for the file sink; required when outputs includes "file". Supports ${CODDY_HOME}.

rotation.description: Size-based rotation for the file sink.

max_size_mb.description: Rotate after the file reaches this size in MB; 0 disables size-based rotation.

max_files.description: Rotated backups to keep when max_size_mb > 0.

sessions.title: Session storage
sessions.description: Where persisted session bundles are stored.

dir.description: Sessions root directory. Empty resolves to ${CODDY_HOME}/sessions. Supports ${CODDY_HOME} and ~.

compaction.title: Context compaction
compaction.description: Summarizes older conversation history so long sessions keep fitting the model context window. Manual compact command plus automatic trigger at a percent of the model's context window.

enable.description: Master switch for compaction (manual command and automatic trigger). Defaults to true.

auto_enable.description: Enable automatic compaction at threshold_percent. Set false to keep manual /compact and the Context popover action available without automatic compaction. Defaults to true.

threshold_percent.description: Auto-compaction fires when the estimated context usage reaches this percent of the effective model's context window (1..100): its max_context_tokens, else the window its provider's model listing reports, else 128000 - the window the web UI context ring shows.

keep_recent_turns.description: How many most recent user turns (each with the agent replies and tool activity after it) stay verbatim; only history before that boundary is summarized. 0 summarizes the whole window. When the window holds no more user turns than this, a compaction keeps fewer: the automatic trigger down to the prompt being answered, the manual command down to none.

model.description: Optional models[].model used for the summarization call. Empty uses the session's effective model.

fallback_models.description: Summarizer models tried in order when the one before them fails (models[].model ids). The session's own model is the last resort whether or not it is listed, so a compaction is not blocked by one unreachable summarizer.

result_eviction.title: Read/grep result eviction
result_eviction.description: Collapses superseded read/grep tool results to short placeholders when building the LLM request (the persisted transcript is never rewritten), so paging a large file or a wide search cannot pin dead lines in every later turn. Only results the model marks (keep_result, or keep:true) or the most recent working window survive; a write to a file invalidates earlier reads/greps that covered it.

enable.description: Master switch for read/grep result eviction. Defaults to true.

keep_recent.description: How many most recent evictable results (read pages, grep dumps) stay intact as a working window. 0 keeps none. The default of 2 keeps a read and a grep live at the same time; with 1, a model comparing two results keeps re-fetching whichever the other evicted.

min_result_bytes.description: Results at or below this size are never evicted (too small to be worth a placeholder). 0 makes every result a candidate.

start_percent.description: Evict only once the estimated context reaches this percent of the effective model's max_context_tokens. Below it the replayed history is sent untouched, so the provider's prompt cache keeps it; a placeholder appearing mid-history invalidates every cached token behind it. 0 evicts from the first result; a model without max_context_tokens always does.

memory.title: Long-term memory subagent
memory.description: Optional memory subagent (implementation in external/memory; enable at runtime with memory.enable).

enable.description: Run the memory subagent on every user turn (needs the memory build tag).

model.description: Exact models[].model id the memory subagent runs on; empty uses the session's model.

fallback_models.description: Memory subagent models tried in order when the one before them fails before answering (models[].model ids). The session's own model is the last resort whether or not it is listed, so one unreachable deployment does not take the memory run down with it.

dir.description: Long-term memory root. Empty resolves to ${CODDY_HOME}/memory. Supports ${CODDY_HOME} and ~.

wait_seconds.description: How long a user turn waits for the memory subagent's report before its first model call. An explicit 0 never waits: the report then reaches the turn only through a later step, or stays in the Tasks panel.

timeout_seconds.description: Hard limit of one memory run in seconds, capped by tools.background.max_timeout_seconds like every task of the pool.

keep_runs.description: Finished memory runs kept per session, task record and child transcript alike; the oldest beyond this number are removed when a run finishes. An explicit 0 keeps every run.

recall_max_turns.description: Bounds the memory subagent's ReAct rounds together with persist_max_turns; the child's cap is the larger of the two.

persist_max_turns.description: Bounds the memory subagent's ReAct rounds together with recall_max_turns; the child's cap is the larger of the two.

copilot_max_tokens.description: Completion token cap for the memory model's calls.

max_note_chars.description: Longest body one note saved by coddy_memory_save may have, in characters (not bytes). An explicit 0 removes the cap.

additional_prompt.description: Operator instructions for the memory subagent alone: a section of its system prompt that the main agent never sees. Empty adds nothing.

additional_prompt_max_chars.description: Cap on additional_prompt in characters; a longer text is cut there, the agent log says so and coddy -t reports it. 0 means no cap.

httpserver.title: HTTP gateway
httpserver.description: OpenAI-compatible HTTP API defaults (used only by binaries built with -tags http; the embedded SPA needs -tags http,ui). See https://coddy.dev/docs/reference/http-api.

enable.description: Serve the HTTP API (and the embedded SPA) in this process. Omitted means true; set false on a node that only polls a messenger or relays a swarm.

host.description: Bind address for the HTTP API. Empty means 127.0.0.1; set 0.0.0.0 to accept connections from other machines.

port.description: Default listen port when coddy serve does not pass -P/--port. 0 falls back to 12345.

auth_token.description: Optional bearer credential for the HTTP API. Empty means no authentication (historical default). Use a "${ENV}" reference to keep the secret out of the file; never echoed back by GET /coddy/config. Prefer --auth-token / CODDY_HTTP_TOKEN to keep it out of config.yaml entirely. See https://coddy.dev/docs/operate/remote.

login.title: Web UI sign-in
login.description: Optional password sign-in for the browser, so a server on a network is not readable by everyone who finds the port. Off unless an account exists here or in CODDY_HTTP_USER / CODDY_HTTP_PASSWORD. API clients keep using auth_token. See https://coddy.dev/docs/operate/remote.

enable.description: Turn the sign-in form on or off explicitly. Omitted follows the credentials: an account here or in the environment enables it. false keeps the form off with the variables still set.

mode.description: How a browser authenticates. Only "password" is implemented; the key exists so a trusted-proxy mode can be added without moving your configuration.

user.description: Account name for the sign-in form. Supports "${ENV}" references, e.g. "${CODDY_HTTP_USER}".

password_hash.description: argon2id hash of the password in PHC form ("$argon2id$v=19$m=...$..."), written by `coddy serve set-password`. Never echoed back by GET /coddy/config, and a save from the settings screen preserves it. Put a plaintext password in CODDY_HTTP_PASSWORD instead of here.

session_ttl_hours.description: How long a browser stays signed in. 0 means the cookie is dropped when the browser closes; the server still expires the session itself after 30 days, because a record it keeps forever is not a session.

public_docs.description: When auth is enabled, keep /docs and /openapi.* reachable without a token.

allow_insecure.description: Silence the two startup warnings about a server without authentication - a non-loopback bind, and CORS that admits pages nobody listed (allow_loopback or "*") - and the --dry-run findings that mirror them.

cors.title: CORS
cors.description: Cross-origin access so a browser UI on another origin can call this API (e.g. the bundled UI pointed at a remote server). Bearer auth still applies: CORS decides whether a browser shows a page the answer, never whether the server gives one.

enable.description: Handle CORS preflight and emit Access-Control-* headers for allowed origins.

allow_loopback.description: Also allow any page served from the browser's own machine: an http or https origin whose host is localhost, a *.localhost name, 127.0.0.0/8 or [::1], on any port. The laptop case of a remote coddy serve, where the web UI comes from the laptop's own coddy serve and its port moves. Narrower than "*", and like "*" only as safe as the token or sign-in behind the API.

allowed_origins.description: Exact origins permitted to call the API, e.g. "http://localhost:5173". A single "*" allows any origin.

remotes.description: Remote coddy serve servers and swarm relays offered in the UI environment selector and resolved by `coddy --remote <name>`. An entry may carry the token to present; without one the UI keeps the token in the browser per remote and the console reads --remote-token or CODDY_REMOTE_TOKEN.

name.description: Display label for the remote. Empty: the web UI shows the name the remote reports (a relay's swarm.name, else the host name it runs on; an agent's host name), else its address.

url.description: Base URL of the remote coddy serve server or relay, e.g. "https://box.example:12345".

token.description: Bearer token to present to this remote: a relay's client token (swarm.auth_token) or a server's httpserver.auth_token, usually a ${ENV} reference. Optional and opt-in: every browser that reads this configuration receives it, and coddy --remote <name> uses it when --remote-token is not given. A node mounted under a relay (<url>/swarm/nodes/<name>) takes the relay's token.

shared_models.title: Shared models
shared_models.description: Serves the models[] rows that carry shared_as to other Coddys: GET /coddy/llm/models, POST /coddy/llm/completions, reachable directly or through a swarm relay mount. GET /coddy/llm/models/{alias}/usage answers the account usage behind an alias as percent used with the seconds to each reset, never the plan, the key name, the wallet or a model id; providers[].usage_limits_panel: false on the lender's provider row answers {"supported": false} to every borrower. The credentials and the limits of those routes are set here; which rows are shared is set on the rows.

tokens.description: LLM-only bearer tokens, "${ENV}" references expanded at load as for auth_token; never echoed back by GET /coddy/config. A token listed here opens only GET /coddy/llm/models, GET /coddy/llm/models/{alias}/usage and POST /coddy/llm/completions and is refused on every other route, where httpserver.auth_token opens the whole API. Any token listed here turns authentication on: with no main token and no login, every other route is closed to every caller. A token cannot also be httpserver.auth_token or a swarm token: the loader refuses it. The tokens of --auth-token / CODDY_HTTP_TOKEN and of the swarm flags are known only to the process, so coddy -t (environment), serve at start-up, a reload and PUT /coddy/config refuse a duplicate of those; a duplicate that reaches the gate is read as a shared-model token (least privilege).

max_streams.description: How many shared-model calls one credential (any token class, or anonymous when authentication is off) may have running at once, all aliases together. A further call is refused at once with 429 kind busy, before anything reaches the provider; the calling Coddy waits for a slot (providers[].busy_wait_ms). 0 or omitted means 5; a negative value is refused. Through a relay the node sees one credential, so the limit then counts every client of that relay together.

rate_per_minute.description: How many shared-model calls one credential may start per minute, beside max_streams. A call past the window is refused at once with 429 kind busy and a Retry-After; the calling Coddy waits for it like for a full slot. 0 or omitted means no limit; a negative value is refused.

rate_burst.description: How many calls may start at once before rate_per_minute applies. 0 or omitted means the rate, capped by max_streams, at least 1. Has no effect without rate_per_minute.

max_call_ms.description: Longest time, in milliseconds, one blocking (stream: false) call of a shared model may run, from the start of the provider call to its result; a call that exceeds it ends as an upstream timeout and frees its slot. Omit for 1800000 (30 minutes). At most 28800000 (8 hours); an explicit 0 means that ceiling, never "no bound". A streamed model is bounded by agent.llm_stream_idle_timeout_ms per gap instead. coddy -t warns about a value above 1800000 together with a shared stream: false model whose provider has no timeout_ms.

tls.title: HTTPS
tls.description: Serve the API over HTTPS, HTTP/1.1 only (so a shared call keeps a connection of its own and the liveness bound applies). Set both files or neither; without them the listener is plain HTTP, which is a reverse proxy's job to wrap. Minimum TLS 1.2; certificates are startup state, so rotating them needs a restart. A request through a TLS terminator or through the swarm tunnel carries no client certificate: require it at the terminator.

client_ca_file.description: PEM bundle that client certificates are verified against. With it the TLS handshake requires a certificate that chains to it and refuses every peer without one (mutual TLS admission at the transport level: Coddy reads no identity out of the certificate, so who may do what is for a reverse proxy). Needs cert_file and key_file. Startup state: changing it takes a restart.

swarm.title: Swarm relay
swarm.description: Stateless relay that nodes register into and that chains into other relays. The relay itself needs -tags swarm and swarm.enable; the join list below is honoured by any coddy serve process, which is what makes an ordinary agent reachable through a relay. See https://coddy.dev/docs/operate/swarm.

enable.description: Run the swarm relay in this process. Independent of swarm.join, which is how an agent registers into a parent relay.

host.description: Bind address for the relay when the CLI does not pass --swarm-host. Empty falls back to 0.0.0.0.

port.description: Listen port for the relay. 0 falls back to 12346.

name.description: Label for this relay in topology views, in /swarm/info and in a child's node path. Empty: the host name it runs on.

auth_token.description: Bearer credential clients present to this relay. A relay reaches every node with that node's own credential, so an unauthenticated relay bound off loopback is a fleet-wide open door and the server refuses to start unless allow_insecure is set. Never echoed back.

pairing_tokens.description: Credentials a node must present to register. Empty closes registration unless insecure_open_registration is set. Never echoed back.

allow_insecure.description: Permit binding off loopback without a client token.

insecure_open_registration.description: Let any caller register a node without a pairing token. Development only.

allow_private_upstreams.description: Hosts a node may advertise even though they resolve into loopback or private ranges, which are otherwise refused so a registration cannot turn the relay into a probe of its own network.

cors.title: CORS
cors.description: Cross-origin access for the relay API. The SPA reaches a relay from another origin by construction, so this usually has to be on. Allow-Headers includes Last-Event-ID so an SSE stream can be resumed through the relay.

enable.description: Handle CORS preflight and emit Access-Control-* headers for allowed origins.

allow_loopback.description: Also allow any page served from the browser's own machine: an http or https origin whose host is localhost, a *.localhost name, 127.0.0.0/8 or [::1], on any port. A laptop's web UI reaching this relay, whatever port its own coddy serve took. Narrower than "*"; the client token still applies.

allowed_origins.description: Exact origins permitted to call the API, e.g. "http://localhost:5173". A single "*" allows any origin.

tls.title: Relay TLS
tls.description: Serve the relay over HTTPS. Set both files or neither. Minimum TLS 1.2; certificates are startup state, so rotating them needs a restart.

client_ca_file.description: PEM bundle that client certificates are verified against. With it the TLS handshake requires a certificate that chains to it and refuses every peer without one, nodes that join included (they present dial.cert_file and key_file). Coddy reads no identity out of the certificate: a client of the relay is told apart by its token. Needs cert_file and key_file. Startup state: changing it takes a restart.

node_tls.title: Node certificates
node_tls.description: How this relay reaches the nodes that registered themselves over a direct address (a node that dials out through the tunnel carries no TLS of its own): the authority their certificates are verified against and the client certificate the relay presents when a node asks for one (httpserver.tls.client_ca_file on the node). A node cannot ask for either itself. A swarm.upstreams entry with a dial block of its own keeps it and gets nothing from this block (they are not merged); one with no dial block gets it. A ca_file here replaces the system roots. The pair is read at each handshake; the CA is read when the node's route is built.

ca_file.description: PEM bundle that the nodes' server certificates are verified against, when they are signed privately. Without it the system roots are used.

cert_file.description: PEM certificate chain the relay presents to a node that asks for a client certificate. Set with key_file.

lease_ttl_seconds.description: How long a registration survives without a heartbeat. 0 falls back to 90; nodes refresh at a third of it.

fanout_timeout_seconds.description: Per-node deadline for an aggregated call. A slower node degrades into a warning rather than stalling the answer. 0 falls back to 3.

upstreams.description: Nodes configured by hand rather than registered, for an agent that cannot run the join loop.

name.description: Node name; becomes a URL path segment, so letters, digits, underscore and hyphen only.

url.description: Origin the relay dials to reach the node.

token.description: Bearer credential the relay presents to this node. Never echoed back.

dial.title: Dial settings
dial.description: How this leg reaches the other side. Relays are expected to live in different networks, so a proxy hop and a private certificate authority are ordinary here.

proxy.description: Route the connection through a proxy: http, https, socks5 or socks5h. Empty falls back to the standard environment variables. Never echoed back.

ca_file.description: Certificate authority used to verify a peer whose certificate is signed privately.

insecure_skip_verify.description: Accept any certificate. For a lab only; every use is logged.

cert_file.description: PEM client certificate this end presents when the other asks for one: a relay with swarm.tls.client_ca_file for a join, a node with httpserver.tls.client_ca_file or a child relay for an upstream. Set together with key_file; read at each handshake.

join.description: Parent relays this process registers into on startup. Honoured whether or not this process runs a relay of its own, which is what lets relays chain.

name.description: Name to claim in that relay. Empty falls back to the host name.

pairing_token.description: Credential authorising the registration. Never echoed back.

advertise_url.description: Where the relay can reach this process. Leave empty to select the tunnel transport: this process dials out and serves its API back over that connection, which is the only way in when the network accepts no inbound connections.

token.description: This process's own bearer credential, handed to the relay so it can authenticate when it proxies. Prefer a credential minted for the relay alone. Never echoed back.

labels.description: Free-form tags shown in topology views.

dial.title: Dial settings
dial.description: How this leg reaches the other side. Relays are expected to live in different networks, so a proxy hop and a private certificate authority are ordinary here.

proxy.description: Route the connection through a proxy: http, https, socks5 or socks5h. Empty falls back to the standard environment variables. Never echoed back.

ca_file.description: Certificate authority used to verify a peer whose certificate is signed privately.

insecure_skip_verify.description: Accept any certificate. For a lab only; every use is logged.

cert_file.description: PEM client certificate this end presents when the other asks for one: a relay with swarm.tls.client_ca_file for a join, a node with httpserver.tls.client_ca_file or a child relay for an upstream. Set together with key_file; read at each handshake.

clients.description: Relay clients with a credential of their own that opens only the shared-model routes (GET /coddy/llm/models, GET /coddy/llm/models/{alias}/usage, POST /coddy/llm/completions) of the nodes they list. swarm.auth_token stays the full class and is not an entry here.

name.description: Label of the client in logs and counters: lower case letters, digits, '_' and '-', up to 32 characters, unique. 'full' and 'unknown' are reserved.

token.description: Bearer credential of the client. A token belongs to one class only: it must differ from httpserver.auth_token, swarm.auth_token, the pairing tokens, the shared-model tokens and every other client's token. Optional when the client is reached by a certificate alone (cert_names). Never echoed back.

scope.description: What the credential opens. shared_models is the only scope: the shared-model routes (the three calls and the probe's ping) of the listed nodes.

nodes.description: Node paths the client may reach: a node name directly below this relay, child/node through a chained relay (at most four hops), or "*" for any node directly below this relay.

max_streams.description: Concurrent shared-model calls this client may hold on this relay. 0 means no limit.

rate_per_minute.description: Calls per minute the relay forwards for this client. 0 means no limit.

rate_burst.description: Calls allowed at once before rate_per_minute applies. Empty takes the rate, capped by max_streams, at least 1.

ui.title: Embedded web UI
ui.description: Controls the bundled single-page UI (only meaningful in binaries built with -tags http,ui).

enable.description: Serve the embedded SPA at GET /. Defaults to true; set false to run an API-only server (the API still requires httpserver.auth_token when configured).

scheduler.title: Cron scheduler
scheduler.description: Cron-driven scheduled jobs (used only by binaries built with -tags scheduler). Jobs are flat *.md files with YAML frontmatter in ${CODDY_HOME}/scheduler (user jobs) and <workspace>/.coddy/scheduler (project jobs, which run once approved); five-field crontab in UTC. A run is a background agent task under the job's own session, which is the job's run history.

enable.description: Run the scheduler daemon and expose the coddy_scheduler_* tools. Can also be forced per process with coddy serve --scheduler (or coddy acp -scheduler).

max_queue.description: Runs in flight across all jobs at once; a due slot past the cap is skipped until a run finishes, and a manual run past it is refused.

timeout.description: Wall-clock limit for one run, as a Go duration (e.g. "30m", "1h30m"); the background task pool still caps it at tools.background.max_timeout_seconds.

project_trust.description: Trust policy for project jobs, the *.md files in <workspace>/.coddy/scheduler that travel with the checkout: "ask" lists them but runs one only once the operator approved that exact file for that workspace (the shield in the scheduler drawer, or POST /coddy/scheduler/jobs/{job_id}/trust?scope=project from a session in it); a job the operator creates through Coddy is approved at once; "allow" runs them like the operator's own jobs; "deny" never runs them. See https://coddy.dev/docs/operate/scheduler#project-jobs-and-trust.

retain_sessions.description: Finished runs kept per job_id (their task records and transcripts under the job session); older runs are removed when a run finishes.

gateways.title: Messenger gateways
gateways.description: Messenger bot adapters (used only by binaries built with -tags gateway, or -tags gateway.telegram / gateway.pachca for one adapter; started by coddy serve alongside every other enabled subsystem). See https://coddy.dev/docs/surfaces/gateway and https://coddy.dev/docs/surfaces/pachca.

enable.description: Poll Telegram in this coddy serve process.

token.description: Bot token from @BotFather. Leave empty to read the TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN environment variable (e.g. via ~/.coddy/.env).

proxy.description: inherit (the default, the same as leaving the key out), none, or a proxy URL: http://, https://, socks5:// or socks5h://, read like providers[].proxy. inherit follows the proxy the environment of the Coddy process names - HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY and NO_PROXY, never for a loopback address; ALL_PROXY is not read. none connects the bot directly and ignores those variables. A proxy URL sends every Bot API request through that proxy; with SOCKS the proxy resolves host names.

rich_messages.description: Use Bot API 10.1 Rich Messages (native Markdown, streamed thinking placeholder, collapsible tool list). Falls back to legacy formatting when unsupported.

admins.description: Telegram user IDs with elevated rights; admins always pass access checks.

default_access.description: Fallback access level for chats without an override: "all", "admins", or "group:<name>".

default_isolation.description: Fallback session isolation for group chats: "individual" (session per user), "shared" (one session for all), "admin" (admins only, shared session).

user_groups.description: Named sets of user IDs referenced from access fields as group:<name>.

user_ids.description: Telegram numeric user IDs in this group.

chats.description: Per-chat overrides; chat_id is negative for groups and supergroups.

mini_app.description: Makes the web UI of this coddy serve the bot's Telegram Mini App. The web UI adapts to Telegram by itself; these keys tell the bot where it is, so it can set its menu button and answer /app with a button that opens the chat's own conversation. Telegram opens Mini Apps over https only, so the web UI has to be published behind a TLS proxy, with sign-in on (httpserver.login). See https://coddy.dev/docs/surfaces/gateway#mini-app.

url.description: The public https address the web UI is served at, for example https://coddy.example.com/. Plain http is accepted only for a loopback host (an offline stand such as tgfake). No fragment: Telegram puts its launch parameters there. Empty: the bot offers no Mini App and leaves a menu button set in @BotFather alone.

menu_button.description: Make the bot's menu button (beside the message field) open the web UI. Turned off, with url emptied or while the web UI asks for no sign-in, the bot puts back the menu button it replaced (a Mini App set in @BotFather, else the commands), as long as the button still opens the address the bot set.

pachca.description: Pachca integration bot adapter: reads the bot's events history and answers through the Pachca REST API. Turn on Save events history (events_history_enabled) in the bot's outgoing webhook settings. See https://coddy.dev/docs/surfaces/pachca.

enable.description: Run the Pachca bot in this coddy serve process.

token.description: Access token of the Pachca integration bot. Leave empty to read the PACHCA_BOT_TOKEN environment variable (e.g. via ~/.coddy/.env).

proxy.description: inherit (the default, the same as leaving the key out), none, or a proxy URL: http://, https://, socks5:// or socks5h://, read like providers[].proxy. inherit follows HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY and NO_PROXY of the Coddy process; none connects directly; a proxy URL sends every Pachca API request through that proxy.

poll_interval_seconds.description: How often the events history is read, in seconds (1 to 60). Pachca answers that method at about five requests per two seconds.

admins.description: Pachca user IDs with elevated rights; admins always pass access checks.

default_access.description: Fallback access level for chats without an override: "all", "admins", or "group:<name>".

default_isolation.description: Fallback session isolation for group chats: "individual" (session per user), "shared" (one session for all), "admin" (admins only, shared session).

user_groups.description: Named sets of user IDs referenced from access fields as group:<name>.

user_ids.description: Pachca user IDs in this group.

chats.description: Per-chat overrides keyed by the Pachca chat id (a thread has a chat id of its own).
